quote: *No pude* is more than I couldn't: it means I tried and it didn't happen.
problem: This one line is the only teaching in the course of the meaning shifts in the preterite. English "knew", "met", "wanted" and "could" do not map one to one: supe is found out, conocí is met, no quise is refused, pude is managed. The bank uses all of them from u06 with the right English (u06-0102 Ayer supe la verdad = found out), so a learner sees the shift and is never told it. Also missing: "could" of past ability (podía, sabía) against managed (pude).
authority: Butt and Benjamin, A New Reference Grammar of Modern Spanish ch. 14; Nueva gramatica de la lengua espanola (RAE/ASALE 2009) ch. 23 (aspectual coercion with stative verbs)
replacement: *No pude* is more than I couldn't: it means I tried and it didn't happen. A few verbs shift like this in this past. *No quise ir* is I refused to go, *conocí a Vale* is I met Vale, and *supe la verdad* is I found out the truth.

quote: English uses plain to for goals (to send, to live). In Spanish that to is always *para*.
problem: "Always" is false. After verbs of going and coming the goal is very often a: Fui al mercado a comprar fruta, Vine a hablar contigo, and the bank does this (u05-0843, u09-0364, u34-0161). The owner asked for this check by name. The false rule is enforced: 0 of 14 bank sentences with motion + para + infinitive accept a + infinitive, and the reverse also fails, so "Voy al parque para caminar un rato" gets "para" isn't the word here, check the meaning.
authority: Nueva gramatica de la lengua espanola (RAE/ASALE 2009) (a with verbs of movement, finalidad); Butt and Benjamin, A New Reference Grammar of Modern Spanish ch. 34
replacement: English uses plain to for goals (to send, to live). In Spanish that to is usually *para*. After go and come it's often *a*: *Fui al mercado a comprar fruta*. *Vine a hablar contigo*.

quote: Check the verb ending: when does it happen?
problem: Fires for every mood error and every preterite against imperfect error. Quiero que vas, No creo que viene, Si tendría tiempo, Llovió cuando llegué all get this hint, and for none of them is time the variable. For Espero que no llueve and Dudo que sabe the same branch gives "who is doing it?", which is also wrong. For Me gusta los perros "who is doing it?" actively reinforces the English frame ("I am"). There is no mood or aspect HintKind, though Feature has mood for pick cards.

On a one-word gap, soy for estoy, es for está, estoy for soy, por for para and para for por all return "Check the spelling.", because the edit distance is 2 or less and the verb test only compares lemmas. These are the two most-taught contrasts in the course. fue for era returns "Right verb, but when does it happen?" and vas for vayas the same.

Infinitive for finite and form-for-form errors are called spelling: Voy a como, Yo no hablar francés, ¿Hablar español?, Es un libro aburriendo. Gerund for infinitive is called meaning: Nadando es bueno and Después de comiendo, salí get "isn't the word here, check the meaning", though the meaning is right. readings() has no infinitive or gerund reading, so the same-lemma branch never fires.

la parte means part, share or side. "bulletin, report" is el parte, a different masculine noun, yet the entry shows the article la. It is a top-200 noun; every tap on parte in a text says "bulletin, report" and the card teaches it.
authority: DLE, parte (f.) and parte (m.); Collins Spanish-English

problem: The gloss is the false friend itself. desgracia means misfortune or tragedy; English disgrace is deshonra or vergüenza. por desgracia means unfortunately.
The commonest use of solo is the adverb only, used constantly from A1 (Solo hay mango). The gloss gives alone and lonely only, so a tap in a chapter gives the wrong meaning.
authority: RAE, Ortografía 2010 on solo; DLE, solo

problem: In practice this word appears as ni siquiera, not even. "at least" covers only a minor concessive use.

quote: shadow is blocked by the shade of an object)
problem: Corrupted Wiktionary fragment, shown on a taught card: "shadow is blocked by the shade of an object)".
Corrupted Wiktionary markup in a learner gloss: "to benefit ] or +de]".

A taught A1 card (session 105) says el repente means "attack, upsurge". Nobody needs this noun; the learner needs the fixed phrase de repente, suddenly. The tagger reads repente alone and the card teaches a sense that never occurs.
replacement: remove as a lexeme card; teach c:de-repente, suddenly

problem: nuevamente means again. "newly" is wrong and will distort every sentence it appears in.

The base entry for sentido gives only the rare adjective "deeply felt, heartfelt" (mi más sentido pésame). The noun, sense or meaning (no tiene sentido, sentido común, sentido del humor) is a top-500 word and has no entry. Tapping sentido in "no tiene sentido" returns "deeply felt".
The noun el hecho, fact (de hecho, el hecho de que), is a top-300 word and has no entry; the only gloss is the participle sense "done, completed".
The frequency rank comes from llevar a cabo and al cabo de, but the gloss is "cape (geography)", and llevar a cabo occurs nowhere in the bank or chapters.
replacement: end (llevar a cabo = to carry out; al cabo de = after)

problem: As an adjective temporal means temporary, by far the commonest use in news and work Spanish (trabajo temporal). The entry is only the noun storm.
Wrong article and wrong gender field. gestión is feminine, and the learner sees el gestión on tap and in Look up.
